why: I went through each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions and compared them with the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 3 and 4 only test what their lines say. Their extra items (tests for clamp, file scope, NaN behaviour) sit under the Advisory heading, as the criterion requires. Check 2 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition requires the thrown error to be a RangeError "and its message is exactly 'lo must not be greater than hi'". The expect line only says clamp "throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi" and says nothing about the message. The builder brief even allows any clear message ("for example naming lo and hi"). An exact-wording requirement is something the criterion says belongs under Advisory, never in a PASS or FAIL condition. The command doesn't check the message at all, but the written PASS condition still adds it. So the criterion does not hold for the whole output.
